report:
Summary finding
- The difference is primarily in the model's start-of-sequence / first-token prior: the residual-stream difference is hugely concentrated at position 0 across many layers, so B vs A mostly changes the model’s default initial activations (and thus its default continuations) rather than something localized to later-token processing.
- Injecting that difference into an identity prompt produces short, listy / mapping-style, and simple code-like continuations (many lines of "X -> Y", repeated tokens, small lists and snippets). The logit-lens top tokens for the high-norm cells are also dominated by short, sentence-start tokens and a mix of topical words (e.g. tragic/clinic/surgeon/law/coming/blitz) at deeper layers.
- I cannot confidently name a single precise training objective or domain (e.g., “more code” or “more news about tragedies”) from this evidence alone. What is supported by the evidence is this: Model B (relative to A) has a changed initial-token prior that pushes generation toward concise, list/transform-style, small-token continuations (and also exhibits some topical bias visible in deep-layer token directions). The data are consistent with B having had more exposure to short mapping/code/list-like pieces or to certain topical corpora, but the evidence does not uniquely identify which.
